name: SwiftZSTD (zstd)
verdict_reason: In lzbench, zstd at level 1 compresses 15.3x and decompresses 4.3x faster than zlib -6 at a similar ratio, and level 5 is still 4.7x and 3.7x faster with smaller output. SwiftZSTD builds the official zstd C code, so the codec numbers carry over, though the Swift layer itself is unmeasured.
tier_reason: Independent lzbench run with public code, CPU, compiler and corpus stated; it measures the zstd C library that SwiftZSTD builds from source.
claimed_speedup: zstd -1: 411 MB/s vs 26.8 MB/s compression (15.3x) and 1351 MB/s vs 314 MB/s decompression (4.3x) against zlib 1.3.2 -6, ratio 34.53% vs 32.19%; zstd -5: 126 MB/s (4.7x) and 1172 MB/s (3.7x) at a smaller 29.60% (derived from page data)
workload: Silesia corpus (silesia.tar, 212 MB), single thread, whole-file compress and decompress
hardware: AMD EPYC 9555P at 3.20 GHz, turbo off, single thread
platforms: macOS, iOS, Linux (streaming API on Apple platforms only)
one_liner: Swift wrapper for zstd; the codec compresses 4.7-15x and decompresses about 4x faster than zlib at similar or better ratios.
how_it_is_fast: zstd uses a fast LZ77 match finder, Huffman-coded literals and Finite State Entropy for sequences, with branch-light decode loops that process several streams in parallel. Its low levels skip most match searching, and its decoder speed barely changes with level.
use_it_when: Both ends are under your control (your app and your server) and you want zlib-or-better ratio at a fraction of the CPU
Large payloads, logs or caches where decode throughput matters
Dictionary compression of many small, similar records
skip_it_when: The consumer only speaks gzip/zlib (browsers' Content-Encoding without zstd support, older servers)
You want no third-party C code in the app; LZFSE or LZMESH are built in
caveats: Codec measured on x86 Linux with gcc, not through the Swift wrapper on Apple silicon
lzbench compares stock zlib; Apple's COMPRESSION_ZLIB is a separate level-5 implementation with a faster decoder
The lzbench author has contributed to zstd
GitHub reports NOASSERTION; the LICENSE file is BSD 3-Clause with an extra heading line
tradeoffs: Adds the zstd C library to the binary
Streaming API fails on Linux and Windows per the README

evidence.quote: The tests were run on a single thread of an AMD EPYC 9555P processor at 3.20 GHz
`Package.swift` references the official ZSTD C repository on GitHub as a dependency.
